hints.title: Write each intersection equation
hints.body: At an intersection the line and curve have equal y-values. Subtract each line from x2+bx+c to make a quadratic equal to zero.
hints.recap: One line-parabola intersection corresponds to a repeated root.
hints.pitfall: Use the discriminant after combining the two equations.
hints.pause: Write the quadratic for the first line.

recall.reminder: One line-parabola intersection corresponds to a repeated root.

hints.title: Use both tangencies
hints.body: The two zero-discriminant equations are (b−2)2=4(c−3) and (b−4)2=4(c+2).
hints.recap: Each tangency supplies a separate condition on the same coefficients.
hints.pitfall: The second line has intercept <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>, so its quadratic constant is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>.
hints.pause: Subtract the equations to eliminate c and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: Each tangency supplies a separate condition on the same coefficients.

hints.title: Eliminate the shared terms
hints.body: Subtract the two tangency equations, expanding carefully so that the common squared and constant-parameter terms cancel.
hints.recap: Subtracting simultaneous conditions can reduce their degree before solving.
hints.pitfall: The requested final quantity is a difference; preserve its order.
hints.pause: Perform the elimination, recover both parameters and check both original tangency conditions.

recall.reminder: Subtracting simultaneous conditions can reduce their degree before solving.

solution:
The first line produces x2+(b−2)x+c−3=0. Exactly one real intersection requires (b−2)2=4(c−3). Similarly, the second line gives (b−4)2=4(c+2).

Subtracting the second equality from the first yields 4b−12=−20, hence b=−2. Then 16=4(c−3), so c=7; the other equality also holds because 36=4(9).

Therefore b−c=−2−7=−9, option A. The leading coefficient stays 1 in both intersection equations, so the zero-discriminant condition indeed gives a repeated quadratic root.
knowledgePattern: Impose two tangency discriminants on one parabola
